title: THE NATION WANTS TO KNOW: THE MANOJ 60TH BIRTHDAY INCIDENT

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
Good evening.
Tonight, ladies and gentlemen, I am asking a very simple question.
A VERY. SIMPLE. QUESTION.
How—
HOW—
does the sixtieth birthday celebration of Manoj, one of India’s finest entrepreneurs, respected family man, pillar of society, devoted follower of the breaking news, fixer of all things broken, and a man whose cool has been studied by leading scientists,
Ladies and gentlemen, How does this person’s 60th celebration
turn into a scene of VIOLENCE, CHAOS AND ALLEGED MUSICAL COERCION?
I have the details.
I HAVE THE DETAILS.
At approximately 10:43 p.m., during celebrations for Manoj’s sixtieth birthday, hired master of ceremonies and notorious prankster RJ Naved Khan allegedly approached two guests standing outside.
Minutes later, one man was on the floor.
Witnesses say he was crying.
The music was still playing.
And somewhere inside—
people continued dancing.
WHO IS RESPONSIBLE?
Tonight, the nation wants to know.
We go first to eyewitness Jai, who was standing beside the victim.
Jai, tell me exactly what happened.
paragraphs: Tonight, ladies and gentlemen, I am asking a very simple question.

does the sixtieth birthday celebration of Manoj, one of India’s finest entrepreneurs, respected family man, pillar of society, devoted follower of the breaking news, fixer of all things broken, and a man whose cool has been studied by leading scientists,
Ladies and gentlemen, How does this person’s 60th celebration

At approximately 10:43 p.m., during celebrations for Manoj’s sixtieth birthday, hired master of ceremonies and notorious prankster RJ Naved Khan allegedly approached two guests standing outside.
Minutes later, one man was on the floor.
Tonight, the nation wants to know.
We go first to eyewitness Jai, who was standing beside the victim.
Jai, tell me exactly what happened.

items.speaker: JAI
items.text: Man… basically we were outside smoking.
paragraphs: Man… basically we were outside smoking.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
SMOKING.
So you admit you were smoking.
paragraphs: So you admit you were smoking.

items.speaker: JAI
items.text:
Man… Naved came outside and said we should stop smoking and come inside and dance.
We said no.
Then he asked again.
We said no again.
Then Naved slapped him.
paragraphs: Man… Naved came outside and said we should stop smoking and come inside and dance.

items.speaker: JAI
items.text: He was crying quite a bit.
paragraphs: He was crying quite a bit.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
CRYING QUITE A BIT?!
Jai, you are describing what sounds like a horrifying scene with the emotional intensity of a man ordering a Careem pick up
paragraphs: Jai, you are describing what sounds like a horrifying scene with the emotional intensity of a man ordering a Careem pick up

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: And what did RJ Naved do after the victim collapsed?
paragraphs: And what did RJ Naved do after the victim collapsed?

items.speaker: JAI
items.text: He told us the dance floor was getting empty.
paragraphs: He told us the dance floor was getting empty.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
We now go directly to our  political correspondent, veteran journalist R. Rajagopalan — Scoop Raja who is outside the courthouse
Scoop Raja, you have been following today’s court hearing. What are your sources telling you?
paragraphs: We now go directly to our  political correspondent, veteran journalist R. Rajagopalan — Scoop Raja who is outside the courthouse
Scoop Raja, you have been following today’s court hearing. What are your sources telling you?

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text:
Arnab, before I begin—
Small Shloka and intro about today being auspicious
paragraphs: Small Shloka and intro about today being auspicious

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: YES YES YES, VERY GOOD, SCOOP RAJA, COME TO THE POINT.
paragraphs: YES YES YES, VERY GOOD, SCOOP RAJA, COME TO THE POINT.

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text: Arnab, my sources are very clear.
paragraphs: Arnab, my sources are very clear.

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text: There is one tea shop opposite Gate Number Three—
paragraphs: There is one tea shop opposite Gate Number Three—

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: SCOOP RAJA, I AM NOT INTERESTED IN THE TEA SHOP!
paragraphs: SCOOP RAJA, I AM NOT INTERESTED IN THE TEA SHOP!

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text:
Arnab, never underestimate a tea shop.
Half of Indian politics happens in Delhi.
The other half happens next to a tea shop.
My information is that the judge asked RJ Naved why he slapped the guest.
Naved reportedly explained that he had asked the gentleman three times to dance and therefore, in his professional opinion, all peaceful options had been exhausted.
paragraphs: Arnab, never underestimate a tea shop.
Half of Indian politics happens in Delhi.
The other half happens next to a tea shop.
My information is that the judge asked RJ Naved why he slapped the guest.
Naved reportedly explained that he had asked the gentleman three times to dance and therefore, in his professional opinion, all peaceful options had been exhausted.

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text:
Bail today.
Two hearings next month.
Seven adjournments.
Three television debates.
One parliamentary question.
Eventually Supreme Court.
Final judgment perhaps 2041.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: You are saying this could continue for FIFTEEN YEARS?!
paragraphs: You are saying this could continue for FIFTEEN YEARS?!

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text: Arnab, by Indian court standards, this is express delivery.
paragraphs: Arnab, by Indian court standards, this is express delivery.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
OSHO?!
Why are you still here?!
Your panel discussion ended yesterday!

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
Yes.
But when you interrupted me yesterday…
I had not finished my answer.
paragraphs: But when you interrupted me yesterday…
I had not finished my answer.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
I know.
I have only now…
arrived at the second half of my sentence.
paragraphs: arrived at the second half of my sentence.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: No, no, no, Osho, we are discussing RJ Naved.
paragraphs: No, no, no, Osho, we are discussing RJ Naved.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
Exactly.
Because the slap…
is not the problem.

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text: Of course the slap is the problem!
paragraphs: Of course the slap is the problem!

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
No.
The slap is only…
the sound…
of two expectations meeting.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
One man expected to smoke.
Another man expected him to dance.
Between smoking…
and dancing…
there was conflict.
And into that conflict…
came the hand.
paragraphs: Another man expected him to dance.

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text: Arnab, with great respect, this will not stand in court.
paragraphs: Arnab, with great respect, this will not stand in court.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
Nothing stands forever.
Not courts.
Not governments.
Not even a man…
Specially after RJ Naved has slapped him.
paragraphs: Specially after RJ Naved has slapped him.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: That is the first useful thing you have said.
paragraphs: That is the first useful thing you have said.

items.speaker: SCOOP RAJA
items.text: My sources say conviction is possible.
paragraphs: My sources say conviction is possible.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
Your sources are outside Gate Number Three.
My source…
is within.
paragraphs: Your sources are outside Gate Number Three.

items.text: SCENE FIVE: JAI HAS A REQUEST

items.speaker: JAI
items.text: Man… can I step out for five minutes?
paragraphs: Man… can I step out for five minutes?

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
NO!
Absolutely not!
The balcony is now a CRIME SCENE!
paragraphs: The balcony is now a CRIME SCENE!

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
THERE WILL BE NO BALCONY!
For the duration of this broadcast, Jai, you will remain INSIDE and you WILL—
…
No.
I cannot believe I am saying this.
You will remain inside…
and you will dance.
paragraphs: For the duration of this broadcast, Jai, you will remain INSIDE and you WILL—
I cannot believe I am saying this.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
We are now joined internationally by someone uniquely qualified to discuss what happens when entertainment goes too far.
Former viral stunt creator.
Cyclist.
Prankster.
Man who apparently spent several years treating oncoming traffic as an obstacle course.
SALEH BOY.
Saleh Boy, welcome.
paragraphs: We are now joined internationally by someone uniquely qualified to discuss what happens when entertainment goes too far.
Man who apparently spent several years treating oncoming traffic as an obstacle course.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
You achieved enormous internet fame through dangerous stunts. You stole chickens. You cycled into incoming traffic. You were chased through villages.
How many views did these videos receive?
paragraphs: You achieved enormous internet fame through dangerous stunts. You stole chickens. You cycled into incoming traffic. You were chased through villages.
How many views did these videos receive?

items.speaker: SALEH BOY
items.text:
Millions.
Many millions.
One time I take chicken—
very good views.
Another time bicycle between two cars—
even better views.
paragraphs: Another time bicycle between two cars—

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: YOU RISKED YOUR LIFE FOR VIEWS?
paragraphs: YOU RISKED YOUR LIFE FOR VIEWS?

items.speaker: SALEH BOY
items.text:
At that time, yes.
Very good business.

items.speaker: SALEH BOY
items.text:
Problem is now…
everybody in village knows me.
I go outside—
they chase me.

items.speaker: SALEH BOY
items.text:
Everybody.
Chicken owner.
Car owner.
Shop owner.
One old woman I don’t even know.
And every time they see me…
this strange music starts playing.
paragraphs: One old woman I don’t even know.
And every time they see me…

items.speaker: SALEH BOY
items.text:
I don’t know.
But when music starts…
I run.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
Saleh…
you think the village is chasing you.
But perhaps…
you are chasing yourself.
paragraphs: you think the village is chasing you.

items.speaker: SALEH BOY
items.text:
No.
Yesterday fourteen people chase me.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
THANK YOU, SALEH BOY.
Finally, somebody on this panel willing to challenge Osho.
paragraphs: Finally, somebody on this panel willing to challenge Osho.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
The bicycle is beautiful because it has no reverse gear.
Just like enlightenment.
paragraphs: The bicycle is beautiful because it has no reverse gear.

items.speaker: SALEH BOY
items.text: My bicycle has reverse when sixteen villagers are coming.
paragraphs: My bicycle has reverse when sixteen villagers are coming.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
One second.
ONE SECOND.
I AM GETTING BREAKING NEWS.
This is extraordinary.
Ladies and gentlemen—
RJ Naved has LEFT THE COURTHOUSE.
I am being told that the Prime Minister has PERSONALLY INTERVENED and a pardon has been secured.
RJ Naved is joining us RIGHT NOW.
Naved!
Can you hear me?!
paragraphs: RJ Naved has LEFT THE COURTHOUSE.
I am being told that the Prime Minister has PERSONALLY INTERVENED and a pardon has been secured.
RJ Naved is joining us RIGHT NOW.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
You walked into court this morning facing serious allegations.
You have walked out tonight a free man.
HOW?
paragraphs: You walked into court this morning facing serious allegations.
You have walked out tonight a free man.

items.speaker: RJ NAVED
items.text:
Very simple.
Modiji likes my elevator prank videos.
paragraphs: Modiji likes my elevator prank videos.

items.speaker: RJ NAVED
items.text:
Big fan.
He told me he watches them whenever somebody from the Congress party starts speaking in Parliament.
paragraphs: He told me he watches them whenever somebody from the Congress party starts speaking in Parliament.

items.speaker: RJ NAVED
items.text:
Apparently one time Rahul Gandhi was giving a speech and he ended up watching seventeen videos of mine on his phone.
Then he called me.
paragraphs: Apparently one time Rahul Gandhi was giving a speech and he ended up watching seventeen videos of mine on his phone.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: And what did the Prime Minister say?
paragraphs: And what did the Prime Minister say?

items.speaker: RJ NAVED
items.text:
He said, “Navedji, very entertaining.”
Then he said, “But next time, no slapping.”
I said, “Sir, understood.”
Then I asked him to dance.
paragraphs: Then he said, “But next time, no slapping.”
Then I asked him to dance.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text: YOU ASKED THE PRIME MINISTER TO DANCE?!
paragraphs: YOU ASKED THE PRIME MINISTER TO DANCE?!

items.speaker: RJ NAVED
items.text:
Arnab, everybody should dance.
This is my philosophy.
Life is short.
Music is playing.
Why are you standing outside smoking?
Come inside!
Dance!
paragraphs: Why are you standing outside smoking?

items.speaker: JAI
items.text: Man, some people don’t want to dance.
paragraphs: Man, some people don’t want to dance.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
NAVED!
YOU CANNOT DESCRIBE ASSAULT AS THE NEXT STAGE OF PERSUASION!
paragraphs: YOU CANNOT DESCRIBE ASSAULT AS THE NEXT STAGE OF PERSUASION!

items.speaker: RJ NAVED
items.text:
Arnab, you have to motivate people.
Look at your show.
You motivate people by shouting.
I motivate people differently.
paragraphs: Arnab, you have to motivate people.

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text:
One uses the voice.
One uses the hand.
Both are simply asking another human being…
to move.
paragraphs: Both are simply asking another human being…

items.speaker: OSHO
items.text: I still have one point left from yesterday.
paragraphs: I still have one point left from yesterday.

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
Ladies and gentlemen, we end tonight with an extraordinary development.
We now have a live transmission from the Prime Minister of India.
Prime Minister Modi, thank you for joining us.
paragraphs: Ladies and gentlemen, we end tonight with an extraordinary development.
We now have a live transmission from the Prime Minister of India.
Prime Minister Modi, thank you for joining us.

items.speaker: MODI
items.text:
Arnabji.
Thank you.
And first of all—
to Manojji—
my warmest wishes on the very special occasion of your sixtieth birthday.
Sixty years is not simply an age.
It is experience.
It is achievement.
And judging from tonight’s events…
apparently it is also a police matter.
I apologise to Manojji for the unfortunate interruption to his birthday celebrations.
A birthday should bring together family and friends.
It should bring laughter.
It should bring happiness.
It should bring dancing.
But dancing must always remain…
voluntary.
I am also told that Manojji has made tremendous contributions through his work, his entrepreneurship, his carpentary skills  and his support for those around him.
For this, we thank him.
To his friends—
please continue celebrating.
To Jai—
perhaps one less cigarette.
paragraphs: my warmest wishes on the very special occasion of your sixtieth birthday.
Sixty years is not simply an age.
apparently it is also a police matter.
I apologise to Manojji for the unfortunate interruption to his birthday celebrations.
A birthday should bring together family and friends.
I am also told that Manojji has made tremendous contributions through his work, his entrepreneurship, his carpentary skills  and his support for those around him.

items.speaker: MODI
items.text:
To RJ Naved—
one less slap.

items.speaker: MODI
items.text:
And to Manojji—
after sixty remarkable years, I wish you health, happiness and many more years surrounded by the people you love.
May the next sixty years be just as memorable…
Happy birthday, Manojji.
Enjoy your evening.
And please—
smoking outside.
Dancing inside.
Slapping nowhere.
Thank you.
paragraphs: after sixty remarkable years, I wish you health, happiness and many more years surrounded by the people you love.
May the next sixty years be just as memorable…

items.speaker: ARNAB
items.text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
RJ Naved.
Saleh Boy.
Scoop Raja.
Jai.
And Osho, who despite repeated requests is apparently STILL connected to our studio.
Tonight we asked one question:
Can a man simply stand peacefully outside a sixtieth birthday party and refuse to dance?
The answer—
IS YES.
The nation has spoken.
Happy sixtieth birthday, Manoj.
Good night.
paragraphs: And Osho, who despite repeated requests is apparently STILL connected to our studio.
Can a man simply stand peacefully outside a sixtieth birthday party and refuse to dance?
